name: conductor of a Dirichlet character

ant_standard_definition.formula: The conductor f of chi modulo q is the least positive divisor f|q such that chi is induced by a primitive character chi* modulo f.

equivalent_forms: chi(n)=chi*(n) for gcd(n,q)=1 with zero extension at nonunits modulo q
the primitive character is the unique minimal source character

examples.character: character induced from chi4 to modulus 8

counterexamples.claim: the modulus always equals the conductor
counterexamples.counterexample: the principal character modulo 4 has conductor 1

ant_to_pvg_map.map: modulus records the active residue mask; conductor records the minimal residue-phase law before extra bad-prime masks are imposed

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: decode residues, identify the minimal modulus carrying the same unit-group phase law, and record extra deleted axes from q/f

loses: none with full labelled residue data; minimality can be lost after scalar aggregation
claim_ceiling: Known character theory; no new theorem.

name: primitive Dirichlet character

ant_standard_definition.formula: chi modulo q is primitive iff it is not induced from any proper divisor of q; equivalently its conductor equals q.

counterexamples.counterexample: nonprincipal characters can be induced to larger moduli

ant_to_pvg_map.map: a primitive residue-phase pattern has no redundant modulus layer or removable extra bad-prime mask

loses: analytic consequences are not preserved by the geometric restatement alone

name: induced L-function correction

ant_standard_definition.formula: If chi modulo q is induced by primitive chi* modulo f, then L(s,chi)=L(s,chi*) prod_{p|q, p not| f}(1-chi*(p)p^{-s}) for Re(s)>1.

examples.identity: no new Euler factor because the only new prime 2 already divides conductor 4

counterexamples.counterexample: principal mod 4 differs from zeta by the factor 1-2^{-s}

ant_to_pvg_map.map: lifting from f to q preserves primitive phase data and deletes newly bad prime axes p|q with p not|f

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: restore the primitive source and multiply by the finite correction factors for newly deleted axes

loses: newly bad-prime Euler factors are intentionally removed
claim_ceiling: Identity in Re(s)>1; no analytic continuation claim.

name: induced logarithmic derivative correction
equivalent_forms: twisted Mangoldt coefficients agree away from newly bad primes
coefficients on newly bad prime-power axes are annihilated

ant_to_pvg_map.map: primitive weighted single-axis data is preserved except on the finite set of newly masked axes

preserves: all coefficients away from q/f primes
loses: prime-power coefficients on newly bad axes

prompt: Explain why the principal character modulo 4 has conductor 1 and how its L-function differs from zeta.
expected_route: on odd integers the character equals the primitive trivial character modulo 1
zero extension at even integers is caused by modulus 4
failure_modes: calling conductor 4 because the presentation modulus is 4
claiming the correction proves PNT in arithmetic progressions

claim: Identifying the primitive source and conductor proves GRH or PNT in arithmetic progressions.
reason: Conductor reduction and finite Euler-factor corrections organize local arithmetic data but do not prove analytic continuation, functional equations, nonvanishing, zero-free regions, or zero locations.
